title: Investigation & action plan for batching fairness regressions causing small-request tail latency spikes
creator: Ava Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed repeated tail-latency spikes for small, low-token requests (~<20 tokens) across hosted and Dedicated deployments. The spike coincided with a rollout of the adaptive-priority batching heuristic (runtime feature flag) plus an autoscaler config change reducing GPU headroom. Impact: elevated p95/p99 for chat and short-completion endpoints, increased customer error retries and two support escalations. This ticket tracks the post-incident investigation, short-term mitigations, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:12 UTC - First alert: p99 for small requests on us-west-2 rose from 180ms to 2.6s. 2026-03-09 02:17 UTC - Notify-oncall and team pager. 2026-03-09 02:25 UTC - Temporary rollback of autoscaler headroom applied (scaled up pools). 2026-03-09 03:05 UTC - Reproduced locally with synthetic mix; observed batch formation stalls when high-throughput long requests saturated batch windows. 2026-03-09 06:40 UTC - Disabled adaptive-priority heuristic as emergency mitigation. 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC - Root cause hypothesis validated: interaction between adaptive-priority lease logic and reduced GPU headroom created starvation for short-request lanes.
root_cause: Combination of two changes: 1) the new adaptive-priority batching mode deprioritized small/short requests to favor throughput for long-running token streams; 2) a recent autoscaler config reduced reserved headroom on some Dedicated pools, leaving no capacity buffer when a burst of long requests arrived. The batcher backpressure code did not preempt a partially-filled batch when a higher-priority small request sat behind a long request stream, causing batch formation stalls and queuing in the request router.
mitigations: 1) Emergency: reverted adaptive-priority to conservative defaults and re-enabled short-request affinity (2026-03-09). 2) Increased autoscaler min-headroom for affected Dedicated pools (2026-03-09). 3) Temporary alert created for per-tenant small-request p99 > 800ms (Grafana alert).
action_items: A1: Add per-tenant 'short-request' queue and strict preemption path in the batcher runtime. Owner: Lucas Kim. Due: 2026-03-20. Estimate: 5 pts. Status: in progress.
A2: Add synthetic e2e test harness that mixes long-token streams with short requests to catch starvation patterns. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Due: 2026-03-17. Estimate: 3 pts.
A3: Rework adaptive-priority heuristic to include explicit fairness window and max-wait threshold for small requests. Owner: Priya Shah. Due: 2026-03-24. Estimate: 5 pts.
A4: Increase Dedicated autoscaler min-headroom default and add a safety buffer for bursty workloads; coordinate with capacity team. Owner: Maria Gonzales. Due: 2026-03-18. Estimate: 2 pts.
A5: Instrument batch formation timeline in tracing (enqueue -> batch-formed -> sent) and add p99/trace links to Console. Owner: SRE Team (lead: Nikhil Rao). Due: 2026-03-22. Estimate: 3 pts.
A6: Create a canary & rollout gating checklist for batching heuristics with perf/regression smoke tests before enabling on production. Owner: Eng Release Team. Due: 2026-03-19. Estimate: 1 pt.
A7: Postmortem doc & runbook update capturing detection steps and emergency rollback playbook. Owner: Ava Patel. Due: 2026-03-16. Estimate: 1 pt.
A8: Add a Grafana dashboard tile per-customer showing '% small requests starved' and alert when >1% in 5m. Owner: Observability (lead: Kim Tran). Due: 2026-03-21. Estimate: 2 pts.
